As a coastal hub in southeast Florida with a metropolitan population of 6.39 million, Miami functions as a natural gateway between the United States, the Caribbean, and Latin America. whatHappening: Miami Spice Restaurant Month is returning for its 25th edition, running August 1 through September 30, 2026. The program now features a new reserve tier alongside its traditional three-course prix-fixe menus, with more than 300 participating restaurants offering minimum 30% savings.
whoInvolved: The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau (GMCVB) is organizing the event, the official tourism promotion agency for Miami-Dade County. The program engages hundreds of local restaurants ranging from casual dining to fine dining establishments across the Miami area.
whyMatters: Miami Spice drives significant foot traffic and revenue to local restaurants during what is typically a slower summer season, while giving residents and visitors affordable access to high-end dining experiences. The expansion to 300 venues and the introduction of a reserve tier signals growing confidence in Miami's restaurant economy and positions the destination as a serious culinary hub.
articleBody:
The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau has announced the return of Miami Spice Restaurant Month for its 25th consecutive year, bringing expanded dining opportunities to the region from August 1 through September 30, 2026. The milestone edition introduces a new reserve tier to complement the program's traditional three-course prix-fixe offerings, providing diners with additional choices at participating establishments across Miami-Dade County.

Miami Spice has long served as a signature summer promotion designed to draw diners to restaurants during the slower warm-weather months. By offering minimum savings of 30% off three-course meals, the program has historically made fine dining accessible to broader audiences while providing revenue stability to participating establishments. According to Miami Curated, this year's iteration will feature more than 300 participating restaurants, representing a substantial roster of venues ranging from casual neighborhood spots to prestigious fine dining destinations.

The addition of a reserve tier marks a notable evolution for the program. This new category appears designed to accommodate higher-end establishments and offer premium experiences within the Miami Spice framework, potentially attracting diners seeking upscale culinary offerings at discounted rates. The specifics of how the reserve tier pricing and participation structure differs from traditional Miami Spice menus remain central to understanding this year's expansion.

The two-month window from August through September positions Miami Spice squarely in the summer and early fall period, traditionally a quieter season for hospitality in South Florida due to heat, humidity, and vacation patterns. By concentrating the promotion during this interval, the GMCVB helps sustain restaurant activity when tourism and local dining typically dip, supporting both employment and tax revenue across the hospitality sector.

The milestone 25th edition underscores Miami's maturation as a dining destination. The growth from previous years' participation to more than 300 venues suggests deepening buy-in from the restaurant community and confidence in the program's ability to drive meaningful customer traffic. For visitors planning trips to Miami during the promotion period, the expanded options and new reserve tier provide more opportunities to experience the region's diverse culinary landscape at favorable price points.

title: Where Elegance Lives: 5 Wonderful Miami Bars
summary: One of my go-to spots when I’m in New York City is the iconic King Cole Bar at the St. Regis. Stepping inside always feels like an immersion into a bygone era—a time when elegance was a deeply desired way of life. Even as modern fashion has shifted toward the casual, the bar…
whatHappening: Miami Curated has published a guide to five elegant bars in Miami, drawing inspiration from iconic establishments like the King Cole Bar at the St. Regis in New York City. The piece explores venues that prioritize sophistication and timeless design in an era increasingly dominated by casual aesthetics.
whoInvolved: Miami Curated is the publication behind the guide. The piece references the King Cole Bar at the St. Regis New York, a luxury hotel landmark completed in 1904 and currently operated by Marriott International, which holds Forbes five-star and AAA five-diamond ratings.
whyMatters: The article speaks to a persistent appetite for elegance and refined hospitality amid broader cultural shifts toward informality. For Miami's bar scene and the hospitality industry more broadly, curated recommendations of high-end venues help shape destination perception and support establishments that prioritize design and atmosphere over trendiness.
articleBody:
Miami Curated has released a new guide highlighting five bars that exemplify elegance and sophistication, offering a counterpoint to the casual aesthetic that has dominated modern culture. The piece draws its inspiration partly from the iconic King Cole Bar at the St. Regis in New York City, a space that the author describes as an immersion into a bygone era when elegance was a deeply desired way of life.

The King Cole Bar, housed within the St. Regis New York at 2 East 55th Street in Midtown Manhattan, stands as a benchmark for refined hospitality. The hotel itself was originally developed by John Jacob Astor IV and completed in 1904 to designs by Trowbridge & Livingston, with an annex added by Sloan & Robertson in 1927. Now operated by Marriott International, the property holds both Forbes five-star and AAA five-diamond ratings, underscoring its status as a luxury destination. The bar's enduring appeal lies in its commitment to an older standard of elegance—one that contrasts sharply with the shift toward casual dress and informal settings that has characterized contemporary fashion and social culture.

According to Miami Curated, this same philosophy of timeless sophistication informs the selection of five Miami bars worthy of attention. Rather than chase transient trends, these establishments prioritize design, service, and atmosphere in ways that echo the King Cole Bar's approach. The guide recognizes that even as cultural norms have relaxed, there remains a distinct clientele and market segment that values the formality and refinement of an earlier era.

The piece arrives at a moment when Miami's hospitality scene continues to evolve, drawing both locals and visitors seeking destination experiences. By curating venues that emphasize elegance over novelty, the guide offers readers a roadmap to bars where atmosphere and craftsmanship take precedence. Such recommendations serve a practical purpose for discerning patrons while also affirming that refined hospitality—the kind exemplified by institutions like the St. Regis—retains cultural relevance and commercial viability.

The guide ultimately suggests that elegance, while perhaps less fashionable than it once was, remains a viable and valued approach to hospitality. Miami's bar landscape, like that of major cities more broadly, encompasses a spectrum of styles; the existence of venues dedicated to sophistication and design indicates that the market for refined experiences has not disappeared, even as it may have narrowed or evolved.

articleBody:

title: From Casual Lunch to Serious Dinner: Paperfish Sushi Brickell Stepped Up Its Game
summary: Paperfish Sushi Brickell has always been one of my “go to” places to have lunch or happy hour with a friend and they always like it. With all of the sushi restaurants in town you’d ask why Paperfish Sushi? The lovely décor that brightens up your day the moment you walk in,…
whatHappening: Paperfish Sushi Brickell, a casual lunch and happy hour destination in Miami, has elevated its offerings and experience. The restaurant is now positioning itself as a serious dinner destination, signaling a shift in its business model and market positioning.
whoInvolved: Paperfish Sushi Brickell is a sushi restaurant operating in Miami's Brickell neighborhood, competing in a crowded market of sushi establishments. The venue has built a reputation as a casual gathering spot for weekday lunches and after-work drinks among friends and colleagues.
whyMatters: The upgrade reflects broader restaurant industry trends of establishments expanding beyond their core daypart revenue streams to capture dinner service and higher-ticket occasions. For Paperfish, moving upmarket could increase average check size, customer lifetime value, and evening foot traffic in a competitive Miami dining landscape.
articleBody:
Paperfish Sushi Brickell has long served as a reliable lunch and happy hour destination for Miami diners seeking quality sushi in a welcoming atmosphere. The restaurant has built a loyal following through consistent execution and an inviting dining environment that energizes guests upon arrival. However, the establishment is now making a deliberate push to establish itself as a serious dinner destination, marking a significant evolution in its positioning and service model.

The catalyst for this shift appears rooted in recognizing untapped revenue potential during evening hours. While the restaurant has maintained steady popularity during traditional lunch periods and after-work social gatherings, the dinner service window represents an opportunity to serve customers seeking more refined, occasion-based dining experiences. According to Miami Curated, the restaurant's aesthetic appeal—particularly its bright, welcoming décor—provides a strong foundation upon which to build this elevated positioning.

Competitive dynamics in Miami's sushi sector likely influenced this strategic decision. With numerous sushi restaurants operating throughout the city, differentiation becomes critical. Rather than competing solely on casual convenience, Paperfish is leveraging its existing strengths in ambiance and service to pursue customers willing to spend more for dinner occasions such as date nights, business meals, or celebrations. This approach allows the restaurant to serve multiple market segments without alienating its established lunch clientele.

The restaurant's move also reflects changing consumer behavior around dining occasions. Modern diners increasingly seek versatility from their favorite establishments—venues capable of accommodating both quick weekday lunches and more leisurely evening experiences. By upgrading its dinner offerings and atmosphere, Paperfish positions itself as a destination for multiple occasions rather than a single-use venue.

For the Brickell neighborhood and Miami's broader dining scene, this expansion signals confidence in the market's ability to support multi-concept establishments that blur traditional daypart boundaries. Success with this strategy could encourage other casual lunch venues to similarly invest in dinner positioning, ultimately raising the overall caliber of evening dining options in the neighborhood.

articleBody:
The Miami Design District is experiencing a fresh wave of commercial activity as new shops and restaurants open their doors to visitors seeking dining and retail experiences. According to Miami Curated, now is an opportune moment to visit the neighborhood, particularly since major events like the Dolce & Gabbana fashion show and FIFA-related activities have concluded, allowing more relaxed exploration of the district's offerings.

The Miami Design District has long established itself as a premier shopping and cultural destination in the city. The neighborhood is home to over 130 art galleries, showrooms, creative services, architecture firms, luxury fashion stores, antiques dealers, eateries and bars, creating a diverse ecosystem for both commerce and culture. The recent opening of additional retailers and restaurants adds to this already robust marketplace.

The timing of these new openings follows high-profile events that drew significant crowds to the area. Among the new additions are brands that represent fresh concepts for the Miami market, potentially introducing residents and tourists to retailers and culinary experiences not previously available in the district. The specific names and details of these new establishments reflect a strategic effort to diversify the neighborhood's commercial offerings and maintain its competitive position in the luxury and lifestyle retail sector.

For prospective visitors, the combination of established galleries, showrooms, and cultural attractions alongside newly opened venues creates an expanded itinerary. Whether seeking high-end fashion, dining, art, or design services, the district continues to position itself as a comprehensive destination rather than a single-category shopping zone.

title: PASTA: The Model Miami Restaurant
summary: Very reasonable prices, excellent food across the board, very good service, low noise decibel so you can easily talk, PASTA is a dream restaurant which should serve as a model to others in Miami. I'll even go so far as to say it has the best pasta in Miami. And on top of all…
whatHappening: PASTA, a Miami restaurant, is earning widespread acclaim for delivering exceptional Italian cuisine at accessible prices while maintaining the kind of refined service and atmosphere that diners typically expect only at high-end establishments. The restaurant has become a benchmark for quality and value in Miami's competitive dining scene.
whoInvolved: PASTA is a Miami-based restaurant that specializes in Italian cuisine, particularly pasta dishes. The establishment operates under principles of reasonable pricing, attentive service, and noise management that distinguish it from typical competitors in the city's restaurant market.
whyMatters: In a dining market often characterized by premium pricing and overcrowded venues, PASTA demonstrates that restaurants can deliver excellence without sacrificing accessibility or ambiance. Its success as a model establishment has implications for how other Miami restaurants approach the balance between quality, service standards, and customer experience, potentially influencing broader dining standards across the city.
articleBody:
PASTA has emerged as a standout dining destination in Miami, establishing itself as a restaurant worth emulating across the city's competitive culinary landscape. The establishment has garnered attention for striking a rare balance—offering exceptional food quality and attentive service while maintaining a dining environment where conversation flows naturally without the competing noise levels that plague many contemporary restaurants.

According to Miami Curated, the restaurant excels across multiple dimensions that collectively define the complete dining experience. The menu demonstrates consistency in execution, with reviewers noting that quality extends across the board rather than being concentrated in a few signature dishes. This breadth of excellence is particularly evident in the pasta offerings, which have been singled out as among the finest in Miami. The pricing structure remains notably reasonable given the caliber of food and service being delivered, making the restaurant accessible to a broader audience than comparable fine-dining establishments.

What sets PASTA apart in a crowded market is its attention to the full experiential context of dining. While many restaurants focus exclusively on food quality, this establishment has prioritized the acoustic environment—maintaining low noise levels that allow diners to converse comfortably throughout their meal. This seemingly simple consideration reflects a more holistic approach to hospitality than is common in Miami's dining scene, where volume and energy often supersede comfort.

The service standards maintained at PASTA further contribute to its status as a model establishment. Staff attentiveness and professionalism are executed without pretension or unnecessary formality, creating an environment that feels welcoming rather than exclusive. This combination of elements—excellent food, reasonable pricing, professional service, and a well-managed dining environment—provides a template that other restaurants in Miami could adopt to improve their overall offerings.

As Miami's restaurant scene continues to evolve and expand, PASTA represents a valuable counterpoint to the trend toward increasingly expensive, increasingly noisy establishments that prioritize spectacle over substance. The restaurant proves that diners value substance: food quality, service competence, and the ability to enjoy a meal without shouting across the table. For other restaurant operators in the city, PASTA's success suggests that returning to fundamentals—delivering quality at fair prices in a pleasant environment—remains a viable and rewarding approach to the business.
